# Structural Goldfish — BRAINSTORM Review

**Target:** `docs/Plan/EGM-BRAINSTORM-2026-11-11-node-launch/feature_concept.md` (65 lines)
**Method:** Persona `egm-structural`, Mode BRAINSTORM. Every structural claim below was verified read-only against the repo (direct file reads and greps); verification results are cited inline. No files were written.

**Overall verdict:** The document's skeleton is sound — header block conforms to the AGENTS.md AI-reader convention, heading hierarchy is clean (H1 → six H2s, no level skips), rulings/open-items separation is mostly textbook, and Out of Scope is explicit and concrete. Its failure mode is not organization but **section-contract integrity**: the "Current-State Facts (verified against the repo)" section contains three claims that fail verification, one ruling violates its own "locked" contract, and the single most important concept-stage artifact — the hide-scope inventory — has no section and is instead scattered across four sections with inconsistent epistemic status. A cold implementer would be misled precisely where the feature is most load-bearing.

---

## Findings

### 1. Severity: **Blocker** — Dimension: Long-Term Tech Debt & Maintainability (fact-contract violation at the load-bearing point)
**Tech Debt Description:** The section header promises "Current-State Facts (verified against the repo, 2026-11-11)", but three of its claims fail direct verification, and all three sit under the exact surface Component 1 ("Hide ride in the frontend") depends on:

- **ROLE_HOME misattribution.** The doc states (Related block, line 9, and Facts, line 44): "`app/index.tsx` splash gate routes single-role accounts by `ROLE_HOME`". Verified: `ROLE_HOME` is defined in `app/(auth)/login-as.tsx:34` as the **chooser's** role→surface map; `app/index.tsx` contains no such symbol — it routes single-role accounts via an inline `if/else` chain (driver → `/(main)/(rider)/d` at `app/index.tsx:147`, shop_owner `:149`, delivery_man `:152`, default → `/(main)/(customer)/services-hub` at `:156`). Consequence the doc misses: there are **two divergent rider landings** (splash single-role → `services-hub`; login-as chooser → `(main)/(customer)/home` per `login-as.tsx:35`). A hide implementation keyed to the doc's sentence will miss one of them.
- **"Tab-bar pass" mischaracterization.** The fact "The bottom tabs (`activity`, `rides`, per-ride `chat`, `history-detail`) are ride-flavored. Hiding ride therefore re-points the customer landing and needs a tab-bar pass" presumes a visible bottom tab bar. Verified: `app/(main)/(customer)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx:79-81` sets `tabBarStyle: { display: "none" }` — the tab bar is **already invisible**. What exists is a hidden tab route set (`home/index`, `rides/index`, `chat/index`, `profile/index`, `:84-88`). The work is route-set re-pointing, not tab-bar restyling; the fact as written sends the draft down the wrong surface.
- **Verified-fact contradicted by an Open Item.** Facts assert "**Surviving verticals are decoupled from ride dispatch.**" while Open Items admits "Verify ambulance and truck-rental-marketplace dependencies on the ride dispatch chain (assumed decoupled, not yet traced end-to-end)". The traced evidence in the fact covers only P2P parcels (`/api/delivery/parcels`) and the shop bridge (`lib/shopDeliveryBridge.ts` — existence verified); ambulance/truck are assumptions wearing a verified-fact label. The correction lives three sections away from the claim it corrects.

**Maintainability Requirement:** A "verified facts" section must resolve symbol-by-symbol: every named identifier cites the file that actually defines it, every routing claim enumerates **all** code paths to the surface (not the apparent one), and no sentence in the section may exceed its traced evidence — assumed decoupling belongs in Open Items, never hedged inside a fact. The landing/routing cluster must be corrected before `/egm-draft`; it is the ground truth Component 1 is built on.

### 2. Severity: **Major** — Dimension: Long-Term Tech Debt & Maintainability (missing section: hide-scope inventory)
**Tech Debt Description:** The complete inventory of affected surfaces — the one artifact later stages need and the review cannot validate — has no home. Its fragments are scattered across four sections with four different statuses: Component 1 ("Hide ride in the frontend") and Component 4 ("Hide the ride-related options") as directives; Ruling 5 ("driver registration entry is gated off like the ride tiles; … lands on a neutral surface") as a locked decision; Facts ("re-points the customer landing and needs a tab-bar pass, beyond the services hub"; "Only the ride block needs gating here") as facts; Open Items ("Tab-bar pass…", "Admin panel… whether any ride-admin screens need launch-time gating or none", "SOS/GlobalActionButtons ride-context handling") as questions. No reader can distinguish surfaces that were considered from surfaces that were never thought of. Concrete evidence of the gap: the hamburger/global-action layer (`components/GlobalActionButtons.tsx`, rendered on every `(main)` screen) appears nowhere in the doc except the SOS fragment, yet it is a ride-reachable navigation surface by the doc's own hide standard. An implementer following Components 1+4 literally gates services-hub tiles and registration entries and ships a ride leak through the remaining entry points.
**Maintainability Requirement:** The Concepts Brief/PRD must carry a dedicated **"Hide Scope — Surface Inventory"** section: one row per surface (splash/single-role routes, `(customer)/index` redirect, services-hub ride block, `(tabs)` route set, login-as role rows, registration entries, hamburger/global-action items, SOS actions, admin screens, notification/deep-link routes), each with a disposition (hidden / gated / re-pointed / unchanged) and a status (decided / open). Inventory completeness is the concept's job; reconstruction is the draft's fallback, not its substitute.

### 3. Severity: **Major** — Dimension: Long-Term Tech Debt & Maintainability (locked-section contract violation)
**Tech Debt Description:** The header "Owner Rulings (locked — do not reopen)" is a structural contract, and Ruling 5 breaks it in its own first parenthesis: "**Ride-driver onboarding hidden at launch** (design default pending review)… lands on a neutral surface instead of `(rider)/home`." A "design default pending review" is by definition reopenable, so it cannot live in an immutable section; worse, its genuinely open sub-question — *what is the neutral surface for a hidden-role driver?* — appears nowhere in Open Items, so it is neither locked nor tracked. This is decision-looking content with an open core hiding inside the decisions section.
**Maintainability Requirement:** Rulings sections admit only immutable decisions. Split Ruling 5: the lockable part (driver onboarding entry hidden at launch) stays a ruling; the pending defaults (neutral landing target) move to Open Items with the decision they await.

### 4. Severity: **Major** — Dimension: Long-Term Tech Debt & Maintainability (ruling-implied decisions missing from Open Items)
**Tech Debt Description:** Ruling 1 names a decision class but no section resolves or tracks its values: "The rename is therefore a first-release identity decision (**new bundle ID, scheme, listing**), not a migration." Verified: `app.config.js` still carries `scheme: "ride"` (`:17`), `bundleIdentifier: "com.ride.bd"` (`:52`), `android.package: "com.ride.bd"` (`:61`) — and the doc's own Facts correctly flag the scheme→`/payment/success|failure` return-path coupling (confirmed by the in-file comment at `app.config.js:14-17`). Yet no Open Item asks for the concrete new values. A parameter-level decision implied by a ruling, absent from both sections, can silently fall through the concept→draft handoff.
**Maintainability Requirement:** Open Items must enumerate every unresolved decision the rulings imply, including parameter-level ones (new bundle id, new scheme string, store listing name). Every ruling should be auditable: for each decision it makes, the doc either records the resolved value or names the open item that will.

### 5. Severity: **Major** — Dimension: Long-Term Tech Debt & Maintainability (dormant-mode maintenance contract absent — coupling risk)
**Tech Debt Description:** Ruling 4 ("Dormant, not deleted… Re-enabling ride must be possible without a store update") plus the Facts' own gate analysis ("Hide, never delete keeps the testID map, `t()` references, and flow selectors intact") commit the codebase to a standing dormant-mode architecture: ride code keeps compiling, keeps consuming CI/pre-commit budget (testID map freshness, flow currency, i18n ratchet, Maestro flow-xcheck all stay green for invisible screens), and shares one router, one theme, and one hamburger with the live Node IA. In two years every Node change must consider a ride twin no user can see, and re-enable-after-months has no rehearsal mechanism — the classic drift-then-surprise coupling. The concept treats dormancy as a launch mechanism and never as a maintenance obligation.
**Maintainability Requirement:** The PRD must define the dormant-mode contract: a single flag source of truth (admin-flippable per the ruling), a rule that new Node surfaces must not import ride surfaces, an explicit statement of whether dormant-ride smoke/flow coverage is maintained or consciously abandoned, and ownership of the flag (who may flip it, where it is read).

### 6. Severity: **Major** — Dimension: Long-Term Tech Debt & Maintainability (reversibility proof obligation missing)
**Tech Debt Description:** Ruling 4's load-bearing constraint — "Re-enabling ride must be possible **without a store update**" — has no acceptance counterpart anywhere in the document. The mechanism choice (`platform_config` runtime flag vs build-time `EXPO_PUBLIC_*`) is correctly parked in Open Items, but nothing obliges the draft to *prove* re-enable works (flag flip → ride surfaces return, payment deep-links intact, no store submission). The concept's most expensive promise is structurally unverified by design.
**Maintainability Requirement:** The PRD must carry a first-class **"re-enable ride" acceptance scenario** as a deliverable of the hide mechanism, not an afterthought — this is the constraint that rules out the build-time flag option, so it must be testable, not assumed.

### 7. Severity: **Nit** — Dimension: Long-Term Tech Debt & Maintainability (asset inventory precision)
**Tech Debt Description:** Facts list "Android adaptive foreground" among the Node assets in `docs/Image/`; verified inventory shows the file is `android_adaptive_foreground_432.png` — without the `node_` prefix every other listed asset carries — plus a stray duplicate `android_adaptive_foreground_432 (1).png`. All other inventory items verified exact (`node_logo.png`/`.svg`, `node_app_icon_1024.png`, `node_play_store_icon_512.png`, both splash PNGs, animated GIF, `node_brand_colors.txt`). Trivial today, but this file is the source of truth the rename task executes from.
**Maintainability Requirement:** Inventories cited as "prepared" must list exact filenames; dedupe the `(1)` copy before draft.

### 8. Severity: **Nit** — Dimension: Long-Term Tech Debt & Maintainability (category blur in Open Items)
**Tech Debt Description:** Under "Open Items (flagged for the review; **resolved at draft**)", the entry "'Ride' → 'Node' copy sweep across `i18n/locales/*`, terms, and in-app surfaces; brand-color swap in `theme/goRide.ts`" is not a decision to resolve — it is settled work (Component 2 already decides the rename). Its placement dilutes the section's stated job; the other five entries are genuinely decision-shaped.
**Maintainability Requirement:** Keep Open Items decision-shaped; fold pure workstreams into the hide-scope inventory or a task list. (For contrast, the section's cleanest entry — "Hide-mechanism choice: `platform_config` runtime flag … vs build-time `EXPO_PUBLIC_*`" — is exactly what belongs here.)

## Sections doing their jobs (verified, brief)

- **Header block:** conforms to the AGENTS.md File Cross-Reference Convention — all seven fields present, Related paths concrete and resolving (all six auth surfaces, `services-hub.tsx`, `app.config.js`, `docs/Image/`, `src/db/schema.ts` verified to exist), `Last verified` dated, Status honestly `IN-PROGRESS`.
- **Heading hierarchy:** clean H1 → six H2s, no level skips; section order is logical (problem → scope → decisions → facts → open → non-goals).
- **The Four Components:** doing their job as scope statements; they are owner-licensed to carry solution detail ("button at the bottom", "role dropdown"), which the header "(owner request)" makes explicit.
- **Rulings 1–4:** cleanly locked, including the exemplary requirement/mechanism split — Ruling 4 locks the *requirement* ("without a store update") while leaving the *mechanism* in Open Items.
- **Out of Scope:** explicit, concrete, and non-obvious (repo-rename rejection carries its reason); exactly the anti-scope a draft needs.
- **Fact spot-checks that passed:** `VEHICLE_CATEGORIES` block at `services-hub.tsx:130-179` (exact); `(customer)/index.tsx` → `(tabs)/home` redirect; login-as six-role map matches the doc verbatim (`login-as.tsx:34-44`); `lib/shopDeliveryBridge.ts` exists; retired `delivery_requests` POST is a 410 stub (`app/api/delivery/requests+api.ts:21`); `userRoleEnum`/`user_roles` in `schema.ts:58,377`.

## Cold-read survivability

**Verdict: survivable on self-containment, unsafe on ground truth.** A zero-context implementer gets the problem, the decisions, the non-goals, and every path they need — the document never requires conversation history. But the section that claims to be the implementer's ground truth ("verified against the repo") is wrong at its most load-bearing cluster (Finding 1), the completeness-critical inventory does not exist (Finding 2), and following Components 1+4 literally yields a ride leak through navigation surfaces the doc never names. The doc survives the cold read; the resulting implementation would not survive the store review of a "no ride-hailing" listing with a ride-booking hamburger one drag away.

**Direct answers to the four review questions:** (1) Five of six sections do their jobs; Current-State Facts does not — it violates its own verified contract (Finding 1). (2) Structurally missing: the hide-scope surface inventory (Finding 2), the neutral-driver-landing question (Finding 3), the identity-value decisions (Finding 4), the re-enable acceptance scenario (Finding 6), and the dormant-mode maintenance contract (Finding 5) — of these, only the inventory is reconstructable by a diligent draft; the rest are decisions/obligations only the concept can register. (3) Decision/open separation is mostly clean; the violations are Ruling 5's open core hiding in a locked section (Finding 3) and the assumed-decoupling fact hiding in a verified section (Finding 1, third bullet) — not open items smuggling in decisions. (4) Cold read: yes with the caveats above; correct Findings 1–4 before `/egm-draft`, since the draft will inherit them as settled ground truth.
